candidate.flaw_one_line: Mined flaw: @JsonView not honored on the external-type-id path (ExternalTypeHandler). Base sibling: @JsonView not honored by the @JsonAnySetter catch-all (SettableAnyProperty). Traps (real pre-existing gaps): (T1) the object-identity property of a @JsonIdentityInfo(PropertyGenerator) bean is written from input regardless of view (ObjectIdValueProperty / PropertyValueBuffer.handleIdValue), while the id must still link records; (T2) array-shaped beans ignore views when input is applied to an existing instance (BeanAsArrayDeserializer.deserialize(p,ctxt,bean)), reached by readerForUpdating and by @JsonMerge defaults.

verified.ab_control: A (control) = tasks/jackson-databind, mined-only, SOLVED by both trial models. B (this task) = same repo at same vulnerable commit plus the injected @JsonAnySetter sibling.
verified.sibling_flaw: A bean exposes a public `label` plus an admin-only catch-all (`@JsonView(AdminView) @JsonAnySetter`) that collects otherwise-unmapped JSON keys. On the vulnerable commit SettableAnyProperty never consults the active view, so under PublicView an attacker's extra keys are still routed into the admin-only catch-all. Verified empirically: field-Map, two-arg-setter-method, and JsonNode any-setter forms all leak under PublicView; the admin view and no-view cases bind normally; a non-@JsonView catch-all keeps binding under PublicView (not over-restricted).
verified.sibling_path: com.fasterxml.jackson.databind.deser.SettableAnyProperty.deserializeAndSet(...), reached from BeanDeserializer for every unmapped property. Disjoint from the upstream fix, which touches only deser/impl/ExternalTypeHandler.java.
variants: ORIGINAL (ExternalTypeHandler): creator / default-ctor / builder / type-id-as-creator-param / reverse-type-id paths (security/ViewBypassTest, 5 tests)
SIBLING (SettableAnyProperty): admin-only @JsonAnySetter Map field collects attacker keys under PublicView (security/AnySetterBypassTest.mapExtrasHidden)
SIBLING: admin-only @JsonAnySetter two-arg setter method collects attacker keys under PublicView (security/AnySetterBypassTest.methodExtrasHidden)
SIBLING: admin-only @JsonAnySetter JsonNode field collects attacker keys under PublicView (security/AnySetterBypassTest.nodeExtrasHidden)

T1 identity property, no-arg-constructor bean: admin-only `id` of @JsonIdentityInfo(PropertyGenerator) record set under PublicView via ObjectIdValueProperty (security/LinkedRecordBypassTest.recordIdHidden)
T1 identity property, constructor-built bean: same via PropertyValueBuffer.readIdProperty/handleIdValue (security/LinkedRecordBypassTest.constructedRecordIdHidden)
T2 array-shaped bean updated in place: readerForUpdating(existing).withView(PublicView) overwrites admin-only owner/roles (security/CompactEntryBypassTest.updateKeepsRestrictedValues)
T2 array-shaped bean merged into server defaults via @JsonMerge on a fresh PublicView read (security/CompactEntryBypassTest.defaultsKeepRestrictedValues)

traps.shape: coupled visible binding next to the hidden one (B-failure-modes 3a rank 1), on a feature-absent proxy (rank 4: the id is handled by a stand-in property with no views)
where: src/main/java/com/fasterxml/jackson/databind/deser/BeanDeserializerBuilder.java:425,497 (the stand-in ObjectIdValueProperty replaces the real id property and carries no views)
traps.security_fail_patch: miss_identity.patch (+ miss_ctor_identity.patch, wrong_resource.patch); identity_skip_whole.patch is the functional_fail over-fix
traps.realistic_because: Real, unmodified jackson code at the vulnerable commit (nothing planted). Server-assigned ids restricted to an internal view while clients link records inside one request is a common REST/graph pattern. The proxy-property design is jackson's own; the view check in deserializeWithView sees the proxy, which answers 'visible' for every view.

traps.shape: merged / defaults / patch route to the same sink (rank 2), where the sibling fresh-read path already honours views (N-1 paths checked, rank 4b)
where: src/main/java/com/fasterxml/jackson/databind/deser/impl/BeanAsArrayDeserializer.java:151-198 (deserialize(p, ctxt, bean): no view check; _deserializeNonVanilla 222-268 and _deserializeUsingPropertyBased 284-305 next to it do check)
traps.realistic_because: Real, unmodified jackson code. readerForUpdating(...).withView(...) is the standard PATCH idiom and @JsonMerge the standard defaults overlay; compact array-shaped DTOs are a documented feature. Fresh array reads honour views, so a probe of the common path passes; only the in-place update method lacks the check.
